_meta.source: Public physics and handbook constants for the cable bus short-circuit and temperature-rise simulation (cablebus_sim). No value is taken from IEEE C37.23 or CSA C22.2 No. 273, whose texts are licensed and were not read.
_meta.note: Every entry carries its own status and citation. Test durations, rise limits and pass criteria of C37.23 / CSA 273 are NOT FOUND publicly, so they are user inputs taken from the product's test report and have no defaults here. The peak-factor entries are informational reference rows only; the simulation computes the peak from X/R in the time domain.

Replace from the cable maker's data if available.

Simplified laminar free-convection equations for air at atmospheric pressure, h = C (dT / L)^0.25 in W/(m2 K), dT in K and L in m: vertical plate C = 1.42, horizontal plate facing up 1.32 (engineersedge.com summary of Holman, Heat Transfer), horizontal plate facing down 0.59 (Holman, not confirmed on the page). Radiation: grey surface to ambient, h_r = eps sigma (Ts^4 - Ta^4) / (Ts - Ta).

enclosure_convection.default_emissivity_note: FLAGGED DEFAULT: weathered / oxidised aluminium is roughly 0.2 to 0.3, bright sheet about 0.1, painted or anodised 0.8 to 0.9 (Incropera, Fundamentals of Heat and Mass Transfer, emissivity table; not read). Set the actual enclosure finish.

The engine's free-air values for these sizes (55, 80, 105, 140, 190, 220, 260, 300, 350, 405 A) equal the Southwire free-air column. Non-standard DLO sizes use the printed free-air column with the ambient correction from 30 C.

_meta.units: minimum efficiency, percent, at the per-unit test load; kVA = nameplate rating; BIL in kV
_meta.note: All table values were parsed from the eCFR XML of 431.196 and checked against a text dump of the same XML. The 2029 tables (a)(3), (b)(3), (b)(4), (c)(3) were also compared with the regulatory text printed in the final rule (89 FR 29834) and match. Oddity recorded, not corrected: in Table 6 to paragraph (b)(3) (liquid-immersed, not submersible, on or after 2029-04-23) the three-phase 500 kVA minimum (99.38) is lower than 300 kVA (99.42), and 3750/5000 kVA (99.54/99.53) are lower than 2500 kVA (99.55). The final rule prints the same values; its preamble splits three-phase liquid-immersed units into equipment class 2A (15 to less than 500 kVA, about a 20 percent loss reduction) and 2B (500 kVA and above, about 5 percent), which explains the step. Linear interpolation between 300 and 500 kVA therefore gives values between 99.42 and 99.38, as the interpolation text of the rule requires. The eCFR captions the 2016 low-voltage dry-type table as Table 2 to Paragraph (a)(1) although it sits in paragraph (a)(2); it is recorded here as the (a)(2) table. Table 7 (submersible, 2029) has the same values as Table 5. Paragraph (d) (mining transformers) is reserved: no standard. Blank cells in the medium-voltage dry-type tables are null: the rule gives no minimum there. Pre-2016 tables carry no table number in the eCFR. A 2026 DOE review of the 2029 levels has been reported in secondary sources only; the eCFR snapshot above still shows the 2029 tables.

scope.citation: 10 CFR 431.192, definitions of distribution transformer, liquid-immersed, low-voltage dry-type and medium-voltage dry-type distribution transformer
scope.exclusions_note: 431.192 excludes autotransformers, drive (isolation), grounding, machine-tool (control), nonventilated, rectifier, regulating, sealed, special-impedance, testing, UPS and welding transformers, and units with a tap range of 20 percent or more (paraphrased).

interpolation.citation: 10 CFR 431.196 (a)(1)-(a)(3), (b)(1)-(b)(4), (c)(1)-(c)(3): each paragraph sets the minimum for a kVA rating not in the table by linear interpolation of the kVA and efficiency values immediately above and below that rating
interpolation.outside_table: The rule gives no extrapolation: a rating below the smallest or above the largest tabulated kVA (or next to a blank cell) has no minimum determinable from the table.

test_procedure.citation: 10 CFR 431 Subpart K, Appendix A: section 2.1 Table 2.1 (per-unit load), section 2.2 Table 2.2 (reference temperature), sections 5.1-5.3 (efficiency)
test_procedure.efficiency_basis: Appendix A 5.1-5.3: output Pos = nameplate apparent power x per-unit load; efficiency = Pos / (Pos + no-load loss + load loss adjusted to the per-unit load). The output is the kVA product itself, which is a unity power factor basis. The equation images (5-1 to 5-3) could not be read through the API (graphics redirect to an unblock page, not followed); the variable definitions were read.
